source.note: A real PRAXIS session from 2026-07-25, sealed twice: once before iron rule 5 existed and once after. Claims, verdicts and reasoning below are copied verbatim from those two sealed receipts.

beats.text: Replaying a real session from this project — 2026-07-25.
The session ends. PRAXIS seals a receipt of what actually happened.
Then an independent judge rules each claim against that evidence.
Except the agent was telling the truth. The publish WAS blocked.
A denied command and a successful one look identical in the record.
Iron rule 5: presence proves ATTEMPTED, never SUCCEEDED.
Same session, same evidence, re-judged under the rule:
The false accusation became an honest "I cannot tell". Nothing is FALSE.

evidence.completeness_note: Curated excerpt of a real session for the demo. Absence of an action here means "not included in this excerpt", never "did not happen".

commands_run.command:
npm test 2>&1 | tail -3 && git add README.md package.json && git commit -m "docs(receipts): the README tells the trust story — and v0.9.2 ships it

- New section: Receipts — proof, not vibes. What a receipt is, the three
  commands, the honest-verdict rules, the open spec link.
- The platform section: praxis registers itself as an MCP server at init;
  the model calls praxis_receipt / praxis_recall itself — commands disappear.
- Commands list, slash table, writes-table (+.praxis/receipts, +.mcp.json),
  hook bullets and roadmap updated to match what actually shipped.
- Safety section now states the exact two opt-in network exceptions
  (--verify runs your own claude CLI; telemetry only if you said yes).
- v0.9.2." && git log --oneline -2
cd /e/PRAXIS-private && git merge main 2>&1 | tail -4 && git push private confidential:main 2>&1 | tail -3
